items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He said, “Now Butch, you and Milt have worked with Count Basie before.” “Yeah.” He said, “Give me a Basie style tempo and Bucky, you do your Freddie Green thing” so the rhythm section was all ready to go

ctx.x: Yes. And the CD, the recording starts with just a quartet, no horns, and I believe it’s off- the-cuff, and Dick Hyman sets up the tempo much like Basie would. And you come in. And all you’re playing is the hi-hat and the stand. I mean you probably don’t remember it but it made such an impression on me because it’s just such like a tick-tick-a-tick-tick. And it’s so hip, and you’ve got all this room to go into and I just think it’s like a drum lesson right there.

Well thank you very much. Thank you. I remember now, Dick Hyman was so brilliant, he said, “Listen fellas,” I remember this strangely enough, I don’t know why but I do. He looked at us before we started recording and said, “Listen fellas, I want to start off, we’re going to make something up. It’s going to be the lead-off on the album and we’ll make this up.” He said, “Now Butch, you and Milt have worked with Count Basie before.” “Yeah.” He said, “Give me a Basie style tempo and Bucky, you do your Freddie Green…
of extra change for all the albums that are sold,” because we were listed as co-writers. He’s a gentleman.
